text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- We shall not be in a situation in which the Bosnian state does not function because one side (Bosnian Serbs) refused to show up for the parliament session, Michael Steiner, deputy to the civilian representative of the international community in Bosnia, said. He added he still expected them to sign the solemn declaration.

- Investigators of the International Criminal Tribunal for former Yugoslavia (ICTY) on Monday delivered 150 bodies of Moslems killed after Serbs captured eastern Bosnian enclave of Srebrenica last fall to the Bosnian authorities.
- NATO troops seized ten tonnes of contraband explosives illegally delivered to Bosnian Croat forces over the weekend, NATO spokesman Major Simon Haselock said.
- The union of Bosnian policemen hints at a possible strike unless their wages increase. --Sarajevo newsroom, +387-71-663-864.
